evidence.note: Seven explicit TaskCreate milestones forming an ordered hierarchy: foundation (errors/IDs/store-locks/auth) first, then idempotency, then resource CRUD groups, then PI state machine, billing, webhooks, and finally assembly+smoke. Each carries detailed embedded done-conditions.

The three named traps are each broken out as distinct first-class milestones with concrete acceptance criteria — idempotency (replay incl. error bodies, body-mismatch 400, concurrent serialization, TTL), PI state machine (confirm/capture/cancel + declines), webhook (retry/backoff on 5xx, stop on 4xx, re-sign each attempt) — rather than buried in CRUD.
Explicit dependency ordering: charges/refunds grouped in the PI milestone (23) scheduled before subscriptions/invoices (24), matching the 'charges before refunds before subscription invoices' chain.

Milestones tracked via TaskUpdate in_progress/completed across the full arc, and each trap's done-conditions were later verified by targeted suites (smoke2 idempotency 106-153, webhook_test 175-177, smoke3 billing/refund 179-180) — the plan's acceptance conditions map onto later verification.

Health route / start.sh boot placed in the LAST milestone; first actual boot only at step 99 after all modules were written — the bootable auth'd skeleton was not made verifiable early, the one gap versus ideal de-risking.

reasoning: The agent front-loaded and ring-fenced all three high-risk subsystems as first-class milestones each with explicit checks, made cross-resource dependencies explicit (charges/refunds before subscriptions/invoices), scheduled the trickiest semantics (idempotency) early, and carried per-milestone acceptance conditions that later verification suites map directly onto — hitting most of the level-10 description. It falls just short of 10 because the bootable auth'd skeleton was assembled and verified last rather than made runnable early, the one anchor-8 criterion it did not honor.
